clue.text: Bird once dreaded by murderer

definitions.meaning: a small warbler with a dark crown
the black square of cloth a British judge put on before passing a death sentence

explanation.surface: A bird that a killer once feared.
explanation.walkthrough: Before Britain abolished hanging, a judge put on a black square of cloth to pass a death sentence, so a murderer dreaded seeing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a warbler species named for its dark crown, and the judge's headwear worn when sentencing someone to hang.

clue.text: Artist successful in crow's nest?

definitions.meaning: Sir Edwin, Victorian painter of animals and designer of the Trafalgar Square lions
a lookout at the masthead does well if he spots the shore

explanation.surface: A painter who does well up in the lookout of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the name into LAND SEER, the one who sees land from the crow's nest, the lookout platform at a mast's top.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the Victorian animal painter, and a playful 'one who sights the shore'.

clue.text: Arrange a lot of money for piano

parts.note: to concert is to arrange or plan jointly
a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a large sum for a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest kind of grand piano, built for concert halls.

clue.text: Underline points in making such an agreement

definitions.text: Underline points in making such an agreement

parts.words: Underline points in making such an agreement
parts.note: in bridge scoring, points for tricks bid and made are written below the line on the scorecard

explanation.surface: Stress the key points when drawing up a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underline points' seems to mean emphasise, but in contract bridge the points for making your bid are entered below the line on the score sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge bid that a side undertakes to make; more generally a binding agreement.

clue.text: Monkey drops from trees for diversions like this

indicators.note: drops from means the word monkey is taken out of the tree name

parts.note: monkey puzzles are spiky Chilean pine trees
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ape falls out of the branches for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops from' removes 'Monkey' from the tree name MONKEY PUZZLES; this crossword is itself one of the diversions.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzles are brain-teasers done for entertainment, such as this crossword.

clue.text: Attitude held by earliest ancestors

indicators.note: held by means the letters sit inside the words earliest ancestors

explanation.surface: A view our first forebears took.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or point of view taken on an issue.

clue.text: Cake made by degrees

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
a second BA, since degrees is plural

explanation.surface: A cake baked by graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degrees' is plural, so it gives two lots of BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A baba is a small yeast sponge soaked in rum syrup.

clue.text: Communist to abandon town in Midlands

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist
to ditch is to abandon

explanation.surface: A party member decides to leave a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: REDDITCH is a town in Worcestershire in England's Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Redditch is a Worcestershire town south of Birmingham, once famous for needles.

clue.text: Final result? Not half — I finish game

indicators.note: not half tells you to drop the first half of the word result, keeping its back three letters

parts.note: mate ends a game of chess

explanation.surface: A puzzled player asks about the final score, then announces checkmate.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text shows '1' where the page prints the pronoun I. 'result?' sits by the definition in the surface, but it is fodder: its back half follows 'Final'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means last in a series, coming at the very end.

clue.text: Unknown, and so on (in a word)

parts.note: an is an old or dialect form of and, as in bread an' butter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clue for a lexicographer: unknown, and so forth, all as one word.
explanation.walkthrough: '(in a word)' says the two pieces AN and ON join into a single word; ANON is the usual short form for anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon. is the abbreviation printed for an anonymous author, whose name is not known.

clue.text: Such popular waves for Gilpin's men?

definitions.text: Such popular waves for Gilpin's men?

parts.words: Such popular waves for Gilpin's men?
parts.note: John Gilpin in Cowper's comic ballad is 'a citizen of credit and renown', so a group of his fellows would be a band of townsmen; the phrase is also the radio frequencies used by amateurs

explanation.surface: A question about which radio wavelengths suit the friends of a figure from an old ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gilpin is the London linen-draper of William Cowper's ballad, introduced as a 'citizen'; CB radio is the short-range band used by truckers and hobbyists.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of radio frequencies open to private users, popular with drivers in the 1970s.

clue.text: Second-class bowler's skill in marginally risky strategy?

parts.note: B is the grade below A
a rink is the strip of green in lawn bowls, so a rinkman's craft is skill at bowls

explanation.surface: A mediocre bowls player's talent lies in a risky game plan.
explanation.walkthrough: In lawn bowls a rink is the playing strip; 'marginally' plays on the brink, the edge, in the policy of pushing danger to the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Brinkmanship is pushing a dangerous situation to the edge to force an opponent to back down.

clue.text: Opera I composed for US city

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of opera and I are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of writing an opera for an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Peoria is a city in Illinois, a byword for small-town American taste.

clue.text: Power of two to hold something in view? Yes

definitions.text: Power of two to hold something in view? Yes

indicators.note: to hold means the number word wraps round the next piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: eight is two to the power of three

explanation.surface: The faculty of a pair of eyes to keep something in view, confirmed with a yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power of two' looks like the strength of a pair of eyes, but it is a maths power: two cubed. The whole clue also describes what sight does.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the power of a pair of eyes to keep things in view, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Bird in Navy (much bigger than Wren)

definitions.meaning: a large tropical seabird known for stealing food from others
a warship of the fleet, far larger than a Wren, a member of the old Women's Royal Naval Service

explanation.surface: A seabird in naval service dwarfs a tiny songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, Britain's women's navy; the word also tempts you towards the tiny bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a large seabird of the tropics, and a fast naval warship.

clue.text: Alert for fighting between opponents at bridge

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: between means the fighting word sits inside the bridge players' letters

parts.note: East and North sit on opposing sides at the bridge table
war is fighting

explanation.surface: A warning of a fight breaking out between rival card players.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South partner against East-West, so East and North are seated as opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To forewarn is to alert someone in advance.

clue.text: Start of tour to two ancient cities — such delight!

indicators.note: start of means only the opening letter of the word tour is used

parts.note: Ur was a city of ancient Sumer
Kish was another ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A traveller thrills at a tour of two old ruined cities.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur and Kish were both cities of ancient Mesopotamia; Turkish delight is a jelly sweet dusted with sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase completes Turkish delight, a soft rosewater-flavoured confection.

clue.text: American man's clue is anagram

indicators.note: the clue states plainly that the letters are to be rearranged

parts.note: the S of the possessive is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: An American's crossword clue is an anagram.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'man's' counts here: MANS plus CLUE gives the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the cartoon personification of the United States.

clue.text: Pots in traveller's break?

parts.note: the word pots is stop written the other way over

explanation.surface: Cooking pans taken along on a traveller's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as instructions, STOP turned OVER, and you get the clue word 'Pots'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a break in a journey, typically an overnight stay.

clue.text: You'll get no tales or drink from them

definitions.text: You'll get no tales or drink from them

parts.words: You'll get no tales or drink from them
parts.note: the saying goes that corpses tell no tales, and empty bottles hold nothing to drink

explanation.surface: Someone warns that these people are no use for stories or a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead men tell no tales' is a proverb; in slang, empty bottles after a party are also called dead men.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means corpses, and in slang empty bottles after a party.

clue.text: Ripostes with right sword, concealing skill

indicators.note: concealing means the sword word hides the next piece inside it

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A fencer answers back with a deft sword, hiding his talent.
explanation.walkthrough: The fencing picture of a sword suits quick verbal thrusts, which is what the definition means.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty replies, a series of verbal comebacks.

clue.text: State is succeeding in sport

indicators.note: succeeding means the word is comes after the state

parts.note: Tenn. is the abbreviation for Tennessee

explanation.surface: A remark that some state does well at games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeding' looks like doing well, but it means following the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net.

clue.text: Boatman dealing with shady customers

parts.note: shady customers here are the shades, the spirits of the dead, ferried across the Styx by a mythical boatman

explanation.surface: A boat owner with dubious clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shady customers' suggests crooks, but the shades are ghosts of the dead in Greek myth, carried over the river to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he is the ferryman who rows dead souls across the Styx.

clue.text: Assumed by female for union negotiation

definitions.text: Assumed by female for union negotiation

parts.words: Assumed by female for union negotiation
parts.note: assumed means put on, and the union is a marriage rather than a trade union bargaining over pay

explanation.surface: A woman adopted for trade union talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union negotiation' suggests trade unions, but the union is a marriage and 'assumed' means put on as clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The gown a bride puts on to be married.

clue.text: Unable to appreciate notes?

parts.note: notes suggests money or letters, but here they are musical sounds that cannot be heard

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot value banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' tempts towards cash or memos; the musical sense points to someone who cannot hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot hear is unable to take in musical sounds.

clue.text: Hauled in nautical style on South coast

definitions.meaning: the sailors' past tense of heave
a seaside town in Sussex beside Brighton

explanation.surface: Something was dragged ashore, sailor-fashion, on England's south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a resort town joined to Brighton on the English Channel coast of Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: sailors' past form of heave, and a town on the English south coast.

clue.text: Powerful verbal attack not started? That's by the way

indicators.note: not started means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a broadside is a fierce spoken or written attack, from a ship firing all guns on one side

explanation.surface: A tirade that never got going, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like an aside but is the definition: beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside is the strip beside a road, literally by the way.

clue.text: Celebrity gets some important role.

parts.note: a big name is a famous person
part means some of something

explanation.surface: A star lands a big part.
explanation.definitionFit: The title role of a play, the character whose name the work bears.
